supersedes: nothing. This is the FIRST anchor declared for hardware_class dev1-macos-arm64, and no anchor from another class may be read into it: docs/bench/adr-051-baseline-local.json was recorded on a developer workstation, which is a different measurement context under config/performance-surface.toml and therefore an answer to a different question.
caveat:
Recorded on the self-hosted Actions runner with the load generator CO-LOCATED with the proxy on the same cores, exactly as the developer-workstation anchor is. It is a REGRESSION anchor and states no capacity; config/performance-surface.toml declares this class slo_declarable = false for that reason.

BOX STATE, stated because it bounds what these numbers are worth. The lane's own settle check admitted the run: 1-minute load 4.97 on 14 cpus at job start, settled to 3.83 after 60s, and the measurement window (07:24:08-07:25:20Z) overlapped no other Actions job on this host. That is quieter than the box the lane refuses to measure on and NOT as quiet as the ~2.5/14 the developer-workstation anchor was recorded at. It shows in the tail: the six reps span p99 19,498-31,604us (+/-24%) against +/-6% for the developer-workstation anchor, while throughput spans 15,483.0-16,599.6 (+/-3.4%). So the throughput floor below is a tight regression band and the TAIL CEILINGS ARE LOOSE — a tail regression smaller than the spread will not be caught here. Re-declare this anchor from a deliberate workflow_dispatch run on an idle host to tighten them; the throughput half does not need it.
